title: Access Verifier: runtime authorization interceptor and unified audit enrichment
creator: Priya Menon
description: Implement an Access Verifier subsystem: a lightweight runtime interceptor that performs RBAC v2 policy checks across API, runtime, and console planes and emits a unified, tamper-evident audit envelope. The subsystem must support attribute normalization from SSO/SAML assertions, staged rollout with canary enforcement modes, decision caching with eviction policies, and structured deny-explain payloads for developer-facing surfaces. The goal is to replace ad-hoc authorizer middleware with a single pluggable component that centralizes evaluation logic, reduces duplicated policy inference, and produces consistent audit records for downstream analytics and compliance.
acceptance_criteria: A single interceptor binary/library that can be deployed in API gateway, runtime worker, and console frontend proxy with a common configuration schema
Policy evaluation calls return deterministic verdicts and a structured explain field containing deny reasons and policy IDs when applicable
Decision caching reduces average policy evaluation latency by at least 35% on synthetic mixed workloads while respecting cache TTL and invalidation hooks
Audit envelope schema documented and emitted to audit-sink with: request metadata, subject attributes (post-normalization), policy decisions, decision-stamp, and integrity signature
SSO/SAML attribute normalization pipeline implemented with mappings configurable per-organization and exercised in integration tests
Canary enforcement mode supports percentage-based enforcement and automatic rollback to allowlist/passthrough on errors
Admin impersonation and emergency-bypass flows are logged with high-severity flags and require a secondary approval token
End-to-end tests covering API -> interceptor -> audit-sink and console flows are added to CI and pass consistently
technical_notes: Approach: implement Access Verifier as a language-agnostic HTTP gRPC-adaptable service plus a small host-language SDK/sidecar for low-latency paths. Core evaluator will use compiled policy rules transformed from our canonical RBAC DSL into an optimized decision graph. Key optimizations: 1) decision stamping to detect reusable decisions across requests; 2) selective KV cache for attribute sets and principal role lookups; 3) lightweight policy sharding based on tenant and resource namespace to minimize evaluation working set. Trade-offs: a central service simplifies logic but adds network hops; mitigate by embedding a hot-path cache in the sidecar and offering an in-process fallback for console where latency critical. Security: audit envelope must include HMAC with rotation tied to KMS. Observability: expose per-decision timing, cache hit/miss, and policy compile metrics. Rollout: start with console and control-plane routes, then expand to public API after 2-week canary.
